item.title: [News] IN SITU: Online Support and Immersive Lab for Emerging Artists Creating in Public Space (3rd Call)
item.description:
IN SITU is now calling for applications from emerging artists creating in public space for their third open call. Around 60 European artists will have access to online content to learn about artistic production related to art in public space from March to June 2027 and an in-person immersive lab with learning and networking opportunities (May to September 2027).

Online content includes:

  • Three online support sessions with On the Move
  • Two to six peer-to-peer exchange sessions with experienced IN SITU artists
  • Short videos and online webinars to learn from IN SITU programmers and artists

An immersive lab is an artistic seminar designed for IN SITU emerging artists to provide food for thoughts to nourish their artistic projects. These six-day gatherings take place during an event or festival hosted by one of the IN SITU partners and bring together around 15 artists at a time

This open call is for artistic proposals in development. The project should:

  • have not yet premiered or toured;
  • be further progressed than the ideas stage;
  • be intended for presentation in public space or non-conventional venues;
  • have the potential to be presented to an audience around summer 2028.

The costs covered for the participation in the immersive lab include: a writing aid fee of 1,500 EUR including taxes, plus travel up to 300 EUR roundtrip for air travel, meals, and accommodation. Maximum two artists from a collective can attend a lab.

IN SITU will then directly support around 10 of the selected projects with production residencies. The programme will culminate in a FOCUS event in the summer of 2028, taking place in the context of La Strada Graz in Austria.

Deadline: 9 December 2026

More info and apply: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qjTiTVucBt_GBuPNP3FY6NOC0Z0Uul8Q/view

item.title: [News] Les Rencontres d'Arles: Curatorial Research Fellowship 2027 (France)
item.description:
Les Rencontres d’Arles is calling for applications from exhibition curators for their Curatorial Research Fellowship to be undertaken throughout 2027.

The Rencontres d’Arles Curatorial Research Fellowship is intended for curators wishing to carry out an original image/photography project. It is supported by Jean-François Dubos. The project chosen will be carried out in two stages.

Research (until summer 2027)

Based on the project selected, the curator will receive a 5,000 EUR grant for expenses and copyright fees throughout the length of the research. The curator will have six months of research time at the end of which he/she will propose a note to the artistic direction of the Rencontres d’Arles to validate the feasibility of the project and its restitution format.

Production (from September 2027)

After approval, if the project is approved by Les Rencontres d’Arles at the end of the 6-month research period, the project will enter the production stage funded by the Rencontres d’Arles.

The 15,000 EUR production budget managed by the Rencontres d’Arles includes:

  • Loans of works
  • Shipping works to Arles (round-trip)
  • Production of the works: printing, framing, wallpaper, videos, etc.
  • An invitation to the curator, and possible costs of the artists’ expenses in Arles during opening week (and/or the mounting of the exhibition)
  • Insurance

In addition to this budget, the Rencontres d’Arles will cover the costs of the exhibition design, the communication, the installation and dismantling of the works, and security.

Deadline: 30 November 2026

More info and apply: https://www.rencontres-arles.com/en/bourse-de-recherche-curatoriale-2027

item.title: [News] Sancy Tourist Office: Horizons 2027 ‘Arts-Nature’ Public Art (France)
item.description:
Horizons ‘Arts-Nature’ in Sancy, scheduled from 19 June to 26 September 2027, is calling for works of ephemeral plastic works created specifically for the Massif du Sancy open-air art exhibition.

The call for projects launched by the Sancy Tourist Office is for the creation of 10 artworks to be installed across the towns and villages of the Massif du Sancy local council community.

First and foremost, this event aims to be an enduring project with a regional flavour that will unite communities and local cultural and tourism partners. The exhibits will be installed at sites that help to highlight the natural surroundings.

Potential sites for the installation of the artworks will be chosen on the basis of the following criteria:

  • The aesthetic and artistic qualities of the site;
  • The diversity of locations available;
  • The proximity of facilities providing access and welcoming visitors.

The sites are made available for the duration of the event. These may be private or municipal properties, with or without the presence of the owner/farmer. They consist mostly of farmland devoted to summer grazing with the presence of cattle, sheep or horses, or to crops that are cut during the season.

An artistic remuneration in an amount of 8,000 EUR including all taxes will be attributed to each artist or group of artists selected including: 6,500 EUR in artistic costs and 1,500 EUR in royalties (recommended proportion). This includes travel costs.

Deadline: 30 November 2026

More info and apply: https://horizons.wiin.io/en/applications/horizons-2027?page-section=general-con…

item.title: [News] Villa Pérochon: Encounters of Young International Photography Residency and Exhibition 2027 (France)
item.description:
The Encounters of Young International Photography Artist Residency takes place in Niort, in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region (France). Niort is located on the edge of the Marais Poitevin, near the Atlantic coast, between Nantes and Bordeaux.

Every year, the Artist Residency welcomes emerging international photographers with a wide variety of approaches, selected based on their portfolios. This year, they will be mentored throughout their stay by the duo Simon Brodbeck and Lucie de Barbuat.

During the Artist Residency, the artists-in-residence agree to produce works that will make up the exhibition marking the end of the Artist Residency, 10 April – 31 May 2027, at the Bernard d’Agesci Museum in Niort.

FAQs

Where is this opportunity?

  • Niort, France

When is this opportunity?

  • 26 March to 12 April 2027

Who is this opportunity for?

  • Emerging international photographers.

What support does this opportunity provide?

  • Artists receive technical support from the team at La Villa Pérochon as well as from two printers at the Picto lab (through a skills-based sponsorship).
  • A technical facility, equipped with professional gear including a black-and-white film darkroom and a digital workshop, is reserved exclusively for them.
  • Expenses covered: round-trip travel from home, supplies needed for the creative process, lodging, breakfast, and dinner.
  • Compensation: a 400-EUR Artist Residency grant + 400 EUR in exhibition fees for the exhibition at the end of the Artist Residency.
Deadline: 15 November 2026

More info and apply: https://www.cacp-villaperochon.com/en/agenda/call-for-applications-encounters-o…

item.title: [News] Indian Ocean Commission: AléVini Regional Mobility Assistance Fund Cycle 7 (Union of Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles and Mozambique)
item.description:
As part of the regional ICC development project in Indian Oceania, the Indian Ocean Commission (IOC) is launching the seventh round of allocation of ‘AléVini, regional mobility support fund’. The project, financed by the French Development Agency (AFD), aims to strengthen regional collaboration and contribute to local economic development linked to the structuring of cultural actors and their ecosystem.

Through this call for applications, the AléVini fund aims to promote inter-island cultural and artistic exchanges to strengthen the ICC value chain (creation, production, distribution and dissemination); and develop the region’s artistic and cultural market by promoting the creation of professional networks. Priority will be given to projects that have an impact on equality by promoting the full participation and inclusion of women.

Eligible activities are networking mobility, creative mobility, or professional development mobility. The initial planned duration of an activity cannot be less than 5 days nor exceed 15 days (excluding travel days) and the mobility activity must take place between 1 March and 20 December 2027.

The applicants must be an individual resident and national of one of the beneficiary countries of the ICC project: Union of the Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles and Mozambique.

Eligible costs include:

Assistance with regional mobility of the individual (up to 3,000 EUR)

  • Inter-island and inter-regional travel costs
  • Living expenses
  • Visa fees
  • Family assistance

Assistance with exporting works (up to 250 EUR)

  • Additional baggage
  • Air and sea freight
  • Customs and transit fees
  • Logistics service providers (freight forwarder, administrative facility, parcel delivery, packaging, insurance, land transport, handling)
Deadline: 8 November 2026

More info and apply: https://kiltir.org/opportunites/alevini-cycle-vii

item.title: [News] ARTEMIS: 2027 Orchestra Academy for Young Instrumentalists (Latvia)
item.description:
This call is aimed at young instrumentalists wishing to take part in an orchestra academy in Liepāja, Latvia, from 28 March to 5 April 2027, at the Great Amber Concert Hall.

The academy will offer a week of training exploring Ludwig van Beethoven’s musical legacy and its connections with European musical traditions, marking the bicentenary of his death. Young musicians will work alongside musicians from the Orchestre des Champs-Élysées, under the direction of Philippe Herreweghe, and prepare a programme in collaboration with a choir of 28 singers, culminating in a final concert at the Great Amber Concert Hall.

The artistic programme will centre on Luigi Cherubini’s Requiem, alongside a selection of classical and contemporary works from Ukraine and Latvia. Through the principles of Historically Informed Performance, participants will explore this repertoire in a collaborative orchestral and choral setting, combining artistic research, interpretation, and ensemble practice.

The programme is looking for 28 singers and 38 instrumentalists from across Europe and eligible neighbouring countries to join the 2027 Artemis Academy in Liepāja.

Eligibility includes:

  • Be 18 years old to 35 years old
  • Be currently enrolled in a music education programme or be recent graduates holding a DEM, Bachelor’s degree, Master’s degree, or equivalent qualification
  • Be nationals of European countries and eligible third countries

The programme provides the following support to selected participants:

  • All artistic activities, rehearsals, masterclasses, and professional development workshops are free of charge
  • Accommodation
  • Travel costs to and from Liepāja

Instrumentalists participating in the Academy in Liepaja may have the opportunity to participate in another Artemis academy in 2028.

Deadline: 5 December 2026

More info and apply: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf6N0CrLS12mSfYK28EQlGFTxCLS-zjlkuKh-4…

item.title: [News] 2200: 2027 Residency for Emerging Artists (Switzerland)
item.description:
2200 gives emerging artists time and space away from their usual routine. Residents live and work on site in Switzerland for about three months and work on a project that grows out of the place.

Alongside the studio, artists receive mentoring on presenting their work and planning exhibitions. Where it suits, artists can conduct an open studio to visitors.

There are three locations as part of the residency: a 1950s post office (Flims, Canton Grisons), a hotel from the late 1800s (Furka Pass in the heart of Switzerland) and a stone warehouse (Ponte Brolla, down south in Ticino). Ponte Brolla will host multiple artists at once and is built for exchange between disciplines.

The residency is mainly for emerging visual artists, but concepts for another discipline which match the site might be eligible.

What is provided?

  • A studio
  • Accommodation
  • A monthly stipend of CHF 500
  • The organisers are also open to discuss in how far they can support travel expenses
Deadline: 31 December 2026

More info and apply: https://2200.ch

item.title: [News] MON-ART: Nicosia Monastery of Arts Residency 2027 in Art, Sustainability and Community (Cyprus)
item.description:
Visual Voices invites applications for the Nicosia Monastery of Arts Residency Programme (in Nicosia, Cyprus) for artists working at the intersection of art, sustainability, and community life. The residency offers space for site-specific artistic experimentation, community engagement, and public showcases.

The aim of the residency is to foster an artist-led regeneration of the Walled City of Nicosia, with a focus on practices relevant to post-conflict contexts. The duration of the residency is from February to July 2027 (6 months) and two artists will be selected.

The MON-ART project is co-funded by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union.

Artist Fee is 6,000 EUR per artist. Shared accommodation, production costs (1,400 EUR), and travel (600–1,000 EUR) are covered by the programme.

Deadline: 23 November 2026

More info and apply: https://monart-5aee4.web.app/residencies#/residencies/visual-voices-walled-city…

item.title: [News] Cove Park: Residency 2027–2028 for Artists in Scotland, UK, Central and South America and Diasporas (UK)
item.description:
Cove Park’s year-round residency programme welcomes local, national, and international artists, creative practitioners, and researchers. The fully funded Awarded Residencies are due to be programmed between May 2027 and December 2028 and can be for as short a time as two weeks or up to three months in duration. Artists, creative practitioners, writers and researchers working in all art forms and at every career stage are welcome to apply.

The Awarded Residencies will be offered to individuals and collaborators who urgently require the time, care, financial support, and facilities offered to develop their creative practice. A final presentation or participation in a public event is not a requirement, but Cove Park aims to support those who wish to work within and contribute to a community of residents, and to benefit from the experience of working alongside others engaged in a wide range of specialisms.

For 2027 and 2028, these residencies are open to individuals, collectives, and collaborative groups based in Scotland and the UK and in Central and South America. Artists from the Central and Sound American diaspora based in Europe and North America are also welcome to apply. People born in Scotland, but living elsewhere in the world, may also apply.

The appointed residents will receive a fee (775 GBP per week), funding for travel (65–1,250 GBP), and, when required, for materials (up to 150 GBP), access support, and the visa application process.

There is also an Application Access Bursary. This funding is for those who experience barriers to the application process due to disability and neurodivergence. This funding can be used to pay a support worker to help with the process (requests to be made by 30 November 2026).

Deadline: 11 December 2026

More info and apply: https://covepark.org/awarded-residencies-2027-2028/

item.title: [News] Mophradat: Residency at BUDA with a Premiere at NEXT Festival 2027 (Belgium)
item.description:
Mophradat is continuing their partnership with Kunstencentrum BUDA and NEXT Festival in Belgium to offer a three-week residency (October/November 2027) for a performing artist from the Arab world. Using BUDA’s facilities and artistic support, the artist would finalise a new production and premiere their work at NEXT Festival at the conclusion of the residency.

Kunstencentrum BUDA in Kortrijk is a space for performing arts, an art house cinema, and one of the largest workspaces for performing arts in Belgium. NEXT Festival is a yearly, international cross-border dance, theatre, and performance festival founded in 2008 featuring works by renowned and young artists in more than 20 locations in and around Lille-Kortrijk-Tournai-Valenciennes cities. It is co-organised by five French and Belgian artistic houses and 18 associated partners.

In addition to complying with the general eligibility criteria, applicants must note the following:

  • Applicants must have developed and presented previous works.
  • Applicants must be working on a new and original project.
  • Applicants must be working with contemporary forms of performance.
  • Unconventional projects dealing with experimental forms and/or concerned with progressive discourses are encouraged to apply.
  • Unsuccessful applicants to previous editions are eligible to re-apply.

Applicants must have advanced and be in the final development phase of their projects by September 2027 and have confirmed co-producers and/or a financing plan, as this residency only partially contributes to the production costs.

Proposals for concerts are not eligible for this call.

The partner covers travel and visa costs as well as residency per diems, in addition to coproduction costs, and a presentation fee for the performance at NEXT Festival for an overall amount of 10,000 EUR, all included. The partners will support the selected applicant through the necessary visa applications; and if the artists are unable to travel due to visa refusals, the project will be compensated.

Deadline: 4 January 2027

More info and apply: https://mophradat.org/program/art-time-residencies/performance/
